question: What is the primary function of a nursery in a community health context?

options.A: Providing daytime care, stimulation, and supervision for infants and toddlers
options.B: Delivering acute inpatient medical treatment for severe childhood illnesses
options.C: Conducting forensic investigations into child abuse and neglect cases
options.D: Offering mandatory primary school education for children over six years old

explanation: Nurseries are designed primarily to provide safe daytime care and developmental stimulation for very young children while parents are at work. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why have community nurseries experienced a significant rise in demand across urban areas of Nigeria?

options.A: The complete eradication of traditional extended family support systems
options.B: Government decrees making nursery attendance compulsory for all newborns
options.C: Increased participation of women in the formal workforce and rapid urbanization
options.D: The mandate that hospitals must attach a daycare unit to every maternity ward

explanation: As more parents move to cities and engage in formal employment, structured out-of-home care through nurseries has become an essential community service. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which type of nursery facility is typically operated within a corporate or institutional compound for employees?
explanation: Institutions and corporations sometimes set up childcare centers directly within their work compounds to support their employed staff. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h2)

question: What is a major regulatory challenge typically associated with home-based nurseries or small creches?

options.A: Maintaining consistent health and safety oversight due to their private residential nature
options.B: Managing excessive financial endowments provided by international donor agencies
options.C: Handling large-scale transport logistics for hundreds of enrolled toddlers daily
options.D: Complying with university accreditation standards for secondary education

explanation: Because home-based nurseries operate inside private residential houses, they often escape routine public health inspections and standard enforcement. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h2)

question: What type of play is most characteristic of toddlers in a nursery setting?

options.A: Competitive academic debating matches focused on verbal reasoning
options.B: Isolated solitary confinement with zero environmental interaction
options.C: Parallel play, where they play alongside rather than directly with peers
options.D: Cooperative team sports requiring complex rule adherence and strategy

explanation: Toddlers naturally engage in parallel play, playing next to other children rather than participating in interactive cooperative games. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h3)

question: A community health nurse observing a two-year-old child in a nursery should expect which developmental capability?

options.A: Writing complex sentences and solving basic mathematical equations
options.B: Exhibiting complete emotional self-regulation without any temper tantrums
options.C: Combining two-to-three-word phrases and walking independently
options.D: Demonstrating advanced fine motor skills like threading small needles

explanation: By age two, normal development includes steady independent walking and early verbal combinations as language skills expand. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why are nurseries considered high-risk zones for infectious disease outbreaks?

options.A: Complete absence of any ventilation or windows in facility buildings
options.B: Immature immune systems and close congregation of young children
options.C: Frequent exposure to toxic industrial waste sites near urban centers
options.D: Mandatory consumption of unpasteurized dairy products at all meals

explanation: Young children possess developing immune defenses and frequently share objects and close contact, facilitating rapid germ spread. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: How does maintaining an appropriate staff-to-child ratio directly impact nursery safety?

options.A: It eliminates the need for routine environmental cleaning and disinfection
options.B: It prevents teachers from ever experiencing normal workplace fatigue
options.C: It guarantees that every child receives a university scholarship upon graduation
options.D: It ensures adequate supervision to prevent falls, injuries, and choking incidents

explanation: Adequate staffing allows caregivers to maintain constant visual and physical supervision, cutting down preventable accidents. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which practice is essential when preparing and serving food to infants in a nursery setting?

options.A: Forcing children to finish every single portion on their plates
options.B: Thorough handwashing and proper utensil sanitization by caregivers
options.C: Using unwashed shared bowls to foster community sharing among peers
options.D: Storing perishable meals at room temperature for extended periods

explanation: Strict hygiene during food preparation prevents the transmission of diarrheal pathogens and foodborne illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h5)

question: When designing nursery meal plans in regions affected by childhood malnutrition, what is the best approach?

options.A: Eliminating all protein sources to reduce the risk of digestive upset
options.B: Relying exclusively on imported processed snacks and sugary beverages
options.C: Restricting dietary intake to clear fluids for the entire duration of the day
options.D: Incorporating nutrient-dense, locally sourced ingredients like legumes and eggs

explanation: Locally available, nutrient-dense foods provide affordable and culturally appropriate ways to combat nutritional deficiencies. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is considered the single most effective barrier against pathogen transmission in a nursery?

options.A: Frequent and thorough hand hygiene for both staff and children
options.B: Applying heavy chemical insecticides to all indoor playground toys
options.C: Administering prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics to every child daily
options.D: Keeping all windows permanently closed to block outdoor air contaminants

explanation: Handwashing physically removes infectious agents from the skin, drastically cutting down the spread of common illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary public health reason for implementing a temporary exclusion policy for sick children in a nursery?

options.A: To curtail the rapid spread of contagious infections among vulnerable peers
options.B: To force families to seek expensive specialist care at tertiary hospitals
options.C: To punish parents who fail to pay their facility tuition fees on time
options.D: To reduce the daily workload for exhausted and underpaid teachers

explanation: Isolating and sending home children with active contagious symptoms protects the rest of the nursery population from infection. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which activity is a core responsibility of the community health nurse visiting a nursery?

options.A: Teaching advanced calculus and grammar to the toddler classes
options.B: Conducting growth-monitoring sessions and checking immunization records
options.C: Managing the financial accounts and tax returns of the nursery business
options.D: Performing major surgical procedures for congenital anomalies on-site

explanation: Community health nurses routinely assess child growth parameters and verify vaccination statuses during facility visits. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h7)

question: How do routine nursery inspections by community health nurses benefit the broader public?

options.A: By ensuring that all children achieve advanced academic literacy before age three
options.B: By eliminating the need for any subsequent home visits by health workers
options.C: By identifying environmental health hazards and training staff on basic first aid
options.D: By converting commercial daycare centres into fully functional government hospitals

explanation: Nurse inspections and staff training improve the baseline safety and health preparedness of early childhood environments. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h7)
